thread:
ana: Quick follow-up from the RFC thread — we observed a prod flake where variant B was evicted mid-request and traffic immediately failed over to the default variant. The fallback handled requests but we lost session/KV continuity and a few streaming calls errored on deserialization. Thinking we need an explicit eviction handshake (lease + probe) rather than immediate cutover. 

ryan: Can you summarize the problem in 1 line? Is it correctness (bad outputs) or availability (errors/timeouts)? :thinking:

ana: Mostly correctness + noisy errors. Long lived streams got partial state and then runtime replaced model weights; the client saw gibberish + closed streams. Non-streaming requests were fine, just slightly higher latency on fallback.

ana: Proposal sketch: when runtime/controller intends to evict a variant, it first marks the variant as EVICTING and issues a short lease (e.g., 20-45s). During lease: in-flight sessions continue to route to the variant; new sessions either go to the stable variant or to a canary routing policy. After lease expiration the controller runs a readiness probe across a sample of instances. If probes pass -> proceed to shrink; if probes fail -> immediate fallback (and emit telemetry).

sasha: Streaming is the hard bit. For streams we can't just reassign mid-stream unless we support token-level resumption or a stateless continuation. Do we have any streaming-resume story?

ryan: Not currently. Option A: sticky-session until stream completes. Option B: force immediate reconnect + resume token that runtime can hydrate. Both have tradeoffs (latency vs complexity).

jamal: Low-friction API proposal for the handshake:
```
POST /api/variants/{id}/evict
{
  "variant_id": "v2",
  "lease_secs": 30,
  "drain_mode": "allow-inflight",    // or "reject-new"
  "reason": "node_preempt"
}
```
Router reacts: set route-state=evicting, honor lease for existing sessions, reject/redirect new ones based on policy.

deploy-bot: deploy log: canary v2 rolled 2026-02-03T03:22Z — 7/12 pods restarted; 3 had readiness flaps then evicted. Fallback to v1 triggered automatically (controller fallback path).

lina: Telemetry note: ~70% of evictions are autoscaler/node preempt. We should consume node drain events from infra and correlate. If eviction reason=node_preempt we might prefer longer lease to let kube drain finish gracefully.

ryan: Two immediate concerns: 1) capacity — allowing in-flight to finish could keep capacity tied up and block cutover; 2) model compatibility — if v2 had a different KV encoding, letting old sessions run could produce inconsistent outputs compared to new sessions. We should consider compatibility shims or schema checks at model load time.

ana: Good points. For capacity we can bound lease with an early-probe path: controller can shrink fraction of traffic during lease (e.g., 10% diverted) to verify fallback correctness while letting most in-flight finish. For compatibility we should add an optional runtime capability: `kv_compat: true|false` — if false then immediate fallback required.

sasha: Small UX/headers suggestion: add a graceful-evict header the router sends to runtimes: `X-Redwood-Evict: lease=30;mode=allow-inflight;probe-url=/healthz/check` — runtimes can surface this to active sessions or start state-sync.

jamal: Implementation note: we should keep the handshake traffic minimal and idempotent. Controller -> router -> runtime state machine: EVICTING -> LEASED -> PROBED -> TERMINATED or ABORTED. Each transition emits an event with correlation_id for debugging.

ana: Ops/telemetry requirements: we need per-variant metrics: evict_reason, lease_seconds, probe_pass_rate, fallback_latency, dropped_streams_count. Also a small sample payload capture when fallback happens to debug KV mismatches.

lina: Agree. Add alert: evictions/sec > baseline AND probe_fail_rate > 5% -> oncall page.

ryan: One more edge: warmup + caching. If fallback variant doesn't have warmed caches (prefix KV or embeddings cache), perf will tank and SLOs break. We should optionally pre-warm fallback during the lease (prefetch hot keys).

ana: Nice. Next steps: I'll draft a mini-RFC with state machine + API + telemetry contract + short proto for the graceful header. Volunteers to review: @ryan, @sasha, @jamal. I'll loop in infra for node-drain hooks. :+1: :rocket:
